mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has declined from -18.3% (t-3w) to -15.9% (t-0w), indicating a stabilization of remote work patterns. This stabilization removes downward pressure on retail foot traffic, allowing RETAIL_REC to recover toward baseline over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 2.4 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days remains below -15% or declines further relative to the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility has remained severely depressed (range -20.7% to -25.0%), indicating persistent commuting avoidance. If TRANSIT does not recover above -15% within two weeks, retail foot traffic will remain suppressed as consumers avoid crowded shopping venues, keeping RETAIL_REC negative.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -15% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -20.7% in t-0w, worst performance in snapshot
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -10% within two weeks AND RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -10%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has recovered sharply from -18.3% (t-3w) to -10.4% (t-0w), signaling seasonal shift toward outdoor activity preference. This outdoor substitution effect will continue to suppress indoor retail-and-recreation mobility over the next four weeks as consumers redirect spending to parks and outdoor venues.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improvement exceeds 5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 7.9 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS mobility reverses to below -15% while RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -10%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has remained stable and positive (1.0–3.0%), indicating essential shopping resilience. When combined with RESIDENTIAL elevation (7.7–9.4%), this signals a home-centric consumption pattern. The interaction of stable essential shopping with elevated residential presence suppresses discretionary retail-and-recreation visits, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains positive AND RESIDENTIAL remains above 7%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -10% while both GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL maintain their current ranges.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has stabilized around -15% over the last two weeks (t-1w: -14.4%, t-0w: -15.7%), indicating a floor in mobility suppression. This stabilization reflects consumer adaptation to current conditions. Absent a shock to TRANSIT or WORKPLACES, RETAIL_REC will remain near this floor over the next four weeks, producing a flat-to-slightly-negative outcome.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC variance only 1.3 percentage points over last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -12% or falls below -18% over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT have both deteriorated sharply in t-1w (WORKPLACES -22.9%, TRANSIT -25.0%), suggesting a policy tightening or infection surge event. If this tightening persists into the forecast period, the combined suppression of commuting and workplace presence will cascade into retail closures or capacity restrictions, driving RETAIL_REC further negative over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT decline more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell 6.8 points from t-2w to t-1w
fact:TRANSIT fell 2.6 points from t-2w to t-1w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both recover above -15% within two weeks while RETAIL_REC remains below -12%.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has remained consistently elevated (7.7–9.4%), indicating sustained home-based activity. Over a one-week horizon, this elevated residential presence correlates with reduced retail foot traffic as consumers minimize external trips. The persistence of this pattern will suppress RETAIL_REC recovery in the immediate week ahead.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has not fallen below 7.7% in any week of snapshot
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below 5% while RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -12% in the next week.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS recovery (from -18.3% to -10.4%) combined with TRANSIT depression (stable at -20.7% to -25.0%) creates a substitution dynamic: consumers shift to accessible outdoor recreation, avoiding transit-dependent retail venues. This interaction will sustain RETAIL_REC suppression over the next four weeks unless TRANSIT recovers sufficiently to restore retail accessibility.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 7.9 points while TRANSIT remained severely depressed
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -15% while PARKS remains above -12%, yet RETAIL_REC fails to rise above -12%.
